title: Path Modifier Architecture, Mathematical Transformations & Extensibility

This archive preserves the project’s original rationale, equations, performance reports and illustrative code. Historical paths, API names, claims and sketches can differ from the current engine. For copy-ready programs use the guides and demos; for current callable signatures use the source-derived API. Performance figures here describe reported experiments, not guaranteed frame rates.

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/PATH_MODIFIER_ARCHITECTURE_AND_EXTENSIBILITY.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/PATH_MODIFIER_ARCHITECTURE_AND_EXTENSIBILITY.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.

This document provides a comprehensive technical breakdown of the **Path Modifier Subsystem** in the Retiam WebGPU Engine. It details the non-destructive geometric processing pipeline, contour data structures, reactive GPU cache invalidation, mathematical foundations of all built-in modifiers, and developer guides for authoring high-performance custom modifiers.

In high-performance vector graphics and mathematical animation engines, vector paths are traditionally static geometries. Retiam's **Path Modifier Architecture** introduces a procedural, non-destructive, stackable modifier pipeline directly coupled to the WebGPU rendering pipeline.

items: **Non-Destructive Geometry Processing**: The canonical base geometry (`_originalContours`) of a [`Path`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Path.ts) is never permanently overwritten. Transformations are computed through a sequential pipeline producing `_processedContours`.
**Deterministic Evaluation**: Each modifier takes a `PathContours` topology and returns a newly transformed `PathContours` topology without side effects on upstream state.

**Reactive GPU Invalidation**: Property mutations on modifiers automatically flag the owning path entity as dirty (`invalidate()`), rebuilding the CPU staging buffers and scheduling immediate WebGPU vertex/storage buffer uploads without requiring manual scene synchronization.

**Dual Extensibility Paradigms**: Developers can extend the engine using lightweight zero-boilerplate lambdas via [`path.modify()`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Path.ts) or production-grade, stateful classes inheriting from [`PathModifier`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/modifiers/IPathModifier.ts).

blocks.code:
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Base Path Definition"
        A["Path Source (SVG, Polygons, Parametric Curves, Shapes)"] --> B["Base Contours: _originalContours"]
    end

    subgraph "Non-Destructive Modifier Pipeline (Path.ts)"
        B --> C{"Modifiers Stack Empty?"}
        C -- "Yes" --> D["_processedContours = _originalContours"]
        C -- "No" --> E["Modifier 0: apply(contours)"]
        E --> F["Modifier 1: apply(contours)"]
        F --> G["... Modifier N: apply(contours)"]
        G --> H["Final Output: _processedContours"]
    end

    subgraph "GPU Synchronization & Rendering"
        D --> I["Path.updateGeometryBuffers()"]
        H --> I
        I --> J["GlobalAnalyticalAllocator / Subdivide Buffer"]
        J --> K["WebGPU Render Pass (Analytical SDF / Stencil Cover)"]
    end

    subgraph "Reactive Invalidation Loop"
        L["Modifier Property Mutation (e.g. modifier.radius = 0.5)"] --> M["modifier.invalidate()"]
        M --> N["targetPath.invalidateModifiers()"]
        N --> O["Mark entity dirty & queue geometry rebuild"]
        O -.-> I
    end

blocks.text: All modifiers operate on continuous parametric 2D contours represented by `PathContours` and `PathContour`:
A complex vector entity (e.g., compound SVG paths, typography glyphs, nested shapes) is represented as a collection of disjoint or nested `PathContour` coordinate streams.
The abstract base class [`PathModifier`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/modifiers/PathModifier.ts) provides standard lifecycle tracking:

items: `targetPath`: Back-reference to the parent `Path` entity.
`enabled`: Toggles modifier execution on/off without removing it from the pipeline.
`isDirty`: Dirty flag tracking changes.
`invalidate()`: Propagates dirty state upstream by invoking `targetPath.invalidateModifiers()`.

blocks.text: Retiam provides [`PathModifierPipeline`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/modifiers/PathModifierPipeline.ts) which can be used completely independently of any entity:

items: `add(modifier: PathModifier): this`: Appends a modifier to the pipeline.
`insert(index: number, modifier: PathModifier): this`: Inserts a modifier at an exact position.
`remove(modifierOrId: PathModifier | string): boolean`: Removes a modifier.
`clear(): void`: Clears the pipeline.
`get<T>(constructor: new (...args: any[]) => T): T | undefined`: Retrieves a typed modifier from the pipeline.
`evaluate(sourceContours: PathContours): PathContours`: Sequentially evaluates all active modifiers, using memoized geometry caching when neither source contours nor modifiers are dirty.

blocks.text: D. Pipeline Integration in Path.ts and PathOptions
In `PathOptions`, modifiers are attached cleanly without redundancy:

items: `addModifier(modifier: PathModifier): this`
`removeModifier(modifier: PathModifier | (new (...args: any[]) => PathModifier)): boolean`
`clearModifier(): this` (alias: `clearModifiers()`)
`setModifier(modifier: PathModifier): this`
`getModifier<T>(constructor: new (...args: any[]) => T): T | undefined`
`modifiers`: Read-only array of attached modifiers.

blocks.text: Retiam includes 11 production-grade mathematical path modifiers residing in [`src/engine/modifiers/path/`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/modifiers/path):

cells.text: Equidistant or count-based contour point redistribution
Hand-drawn wobble, fluid waves, electric vibrations
Adaptive polyline corner filleting with circular arcs
Parallel polygon insetting/outsetting with miter joins
Outline borders, concentric rings, expansion effects
Periodic triangular, sinusoidal, or square displacement
Engineering diagrams, dashed outlines, radar sweeps
Contour vertex and winding order inversion
Pinched stars, blooming flowers, organic morphs
Vortex angular distortion with cubic radial falloff
Converting noisy raw input into smooth curves

blocks.text: Extracts a continuous sub-segment $[s_{start}, s_{end}] \subset [0, 1]$ of the total path arc-length $L_{total}$.

items: When $s_{end} < s_{start}$, the modifier treats the interval as a **wrapped window** $[s_{start}, 1.0] \cup [0.0, s_{end}]$, generating two distinct contours for closed paths.

Arc-length parameterization is calculated via [`PathModifierUtils.computeArcLengths()`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/modifiers/path/PathModifierUtils.ts). Points falling on intermediate cuts are precisely linearly interpolated.

blocks.code:
const trim = new TrimModifier({ start: 0.2, end: 0.8, offset: 0.1 });
path.addModifier(trim);

blocks.text: Redistributes vertices along path contours to achieve uniform spacing:

items: **`byCount`**: Divides the total contour arc length $L$ into $N$ equal intervals of length $\Delta s = L / N$.
**`byLength`**: Places sample points at constant arc-length increments $\Delta s$, preserving geometry density regardless of shape scale.
Guaranteed preservation of closed loop topology.

blocks.text: Applies smooth 2D gradient noise along contour normals and tangents. For vertex $p_i$ with contour tangent $T_i$ and normal $N_i = (-T_{i,y}, T_{i,x})$:

items: Multi-octave fractional Brownian motion (fBm) option for organic turbulence.
Smooth periodic boundary wrap for closed contours.

blocks.text: Replaces sharp corner vertices $(p_{i-1}, p_i, p_{i+1})$ with circular arc fillets:

items: Calculates tangent vectors $v_1 = \frac{p_{i-1} - p_i}{\|p_{i-1} - p_i\|}$ and $v_2 = \frac{p_{i+1} - p_i}{\|p_{i+1} - p_i\|}$.
Evaluates the interior corner angle $\theta = \arccos(v_1 \cdot v_2)$.
Computes tangent cut distance $d = r \cdot \tan(\theta / 2)$, clamped to $d \le \min(\frac{\|e_1\|}{2}, \frac{\|e_2\|}{2})$ to prevent adjacent corner overlap.
Generates a circular arc spline spanning from $p_i + d \cdot v_1$ to $p_i + d \cdot v_2$.

blocks.code:
const round = new RoundCornersModifier({ radius: 0.25, segments: 6 });
path.addModifier(round);

blocks.text: Constructs parallel inset or outset curves at distance $d$:

items: Computes outward/inward segment normal vectors $N_k$.
Computes vertex miter direction $M_i = \frac{N_k + N_{k+1}}{\|N_k + N_{k+1}\|}$ and miter length $L_m = \frac{d}{\cos(\phi / 2)}$.
Protects against sharp corner spikes using `miterLimit`: if $L_m > \text{miterLimit} \cdot d$, the corner gracefully transitions to a bevel join.

blocks.code:
const offset = new OffsetModifier({ distance: 0.15, join: "miter", miterLimit: 3.0 });
path.addModifier(offset);

blocks.text: Generates high-frequency periodic waveforms anchored along path segments:

items: Supported waveforms: `triangle` (sharp teeth), `sine` (smooth ripple), `square` (crenelation).
Frequency specifies wave cycles per unit length or per segment.
Points at original corner vertices are firmly pinned to maintain structural fidelity.

blocks.code:
const zigzag = new ZigZagModifier({ amplitude: 0.08, frequency: 12, waveType: "triangle" });
path.addModifier(zigzag);

blocks.text: Decomposes continuous contours into disjoint dash segments following an array pattern (e.g., `[0.2, 0.1, 0.05, 0.1]`):

items: Traverses arc lengths, alternating between drawing and gap intervals.
Handles offset shifting for running marching-ants animations.

blocks.code:
const dash = new DashModifier({ pattern: [0.15, 0.08], offset: 0.0 });
path.addModifier(dash);

blocks.text: Inverts the topological vertex order of every contour in the path:

items: Reverses stroke draw direction in trim and dash animations.
Preserves contour closure flags.

blocks.text: Radial geometric morph relative to the contour centroid $C = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} p_i$:

items: For any point $p$, radial vector $v = p - C$ and distance $r = \|v\|$.
Intermediate edge samples are displaced radially:
$\text{amount} < 0$ produces a **Pucker** (concave star-burst).
$\text{amount} > 0$ produces a **Bloat** (convex puffy balloon).

blocks.code:
const morph = new PuckerBloatModifier({ amount: 0.6 });
path.addModifier(morph);

blocks.text: Applies angular vortex distortion around a center point $C$ with smooth cubic radial falloff:

items: Smooth $C^2$ continuity prevents geometric tearing at boundary $r = R$.

blocks.code:
const twist = new TwistModifier({ angle: Math.PI * 1.5, radius: 2.0, center: new Vec2(0, 0) });
path.addModifier(twist);

items: **Ramer-Douglas-Peucker (RDP)**: Recursively removes redundant, collinear, or jittery vertices within distance tolerance $\epsilon$.
**Chaikin Subdivision**: Recursively clips corners at $\frac{1}{4}$ and $\frac{3}{4}$ along each segment to produce $C^1$-smooth quadratic curves.

blocks.code:
const smooth = new SmoothModifier({ iterations: 2, tolerance: 0.01 });
path.addModifier(smooth);

blocks.text: Retiam provides two clean patterns for creating custom modifiers:

Best for rapid experimentation, mathematical formulas, or one-off scene animations. Use [`path.modify()`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Path.ts) backed by [`CustomModifier`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/modifiers/path/CustomModifier.ts):
Best for production components, libraries, and reusable motion graphic tools. Inherit from [`PathModifier`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/modifiers/IPathModifier.ts):

Most spatial deformation modifiers (such as `Twist`, `Wiggle`, `Attractor`, `PuckerBloat`) displace existing vertices. If a shape has only 4 corner vertices (like a `Rect`), smooth curved deformation requires adding a `ResampleModifier` ahead of the deformation modifier in the pipeline:

blocks.code:
rect
    .resample({ by: "byCount", count: 180 }) // 1. Subdivide straight edges
    .addModifier(new TwistModifier({ angle: Math.PI, radius: 1.5 })); // 2. Deform

blocks.text: The pipeline executes modifiers in strict index order. Common optimal chains:

items: **Geometric Topology**: `ResampleModifier` (Subdivide edges)
**Spatial Deformations**: `WiggleModifier` / `TwistModifier` / `CustomModifier`
**Corner Treatment**: `RoundCornersModifier`
**Outlines & Stroke Effects**: `OffsetModifier`
**Animation Chopping**: `TrimModifier` / `DashModifier`

Modifiers create new `Vec2` instances for modified vertices. For high-frequency animations running at 60 FPS, avoid unnecessary vertex proliferation by keeping resampling count tuned to the screen resolution.
Calling `this.invalidate()` inside property setters schedules a lightweight dirty check; redundant updates are coalesced per frame tick.
